AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about
matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090
during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Council Member Asatryan met with different departments and staff and thanked them for
  their availability. She attended Concerts in the Park and the installation for the Modes of
  Resistance exhibit held at the Glendale Central Library. She requested that Library and Arts
  and Parks and Recreations departments coordinate the marketing for the summer concerts
  moving forward for residents to have one place to go to see the full staff. She also requested
  staff look into combining cultural events like the Comfort Women’s Day already taking place
  with public facing live music and markets which celebrate and shed light on the diverse
  cultures in Glendale. Asatryan nominated Sona Tatiyants for the Commission on the Status
  of Women, Joseph Kaskanian for the Design Review Board, Marina Manoukian for CDBG
  Program, and Hagop Jack Mavyan for the Audit Committee. Asatryan asked staff for both a
  feasibility study as well as motion options to convert Lot 15 located on Orange between
  Wilson and California into a park in South Glendale which would cater to our residents in the
  08 09 22
  CC
  3
   South Glendale and downtown area who currently have no nearby parks or green spaces.
  Asatryan noted this would be an extremely inexpensive way of utilizing our current city asset
  to add a much-needed park in the area. Devine seconded. Asatryan initiatives to add youth
  seats to the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Commission and the Arts and
  Culture Commission. Brotman recommended to also add youth seats for the Transportation
  and Parking Commission. Asatryan agreed. Brotman seconded. Asatryan requested that
  staff provide a feasibility report and for the RFP the city plans to put out for a consultant for
  Lot 11 Dog park to also include a reconfiguration of the community gardens area at Palmer
  Park for the unused space to be converted into a dog park. Kassakhian seconded.

  Council Member Brotman commended the Economic Development and the GWP
  departments for providing rich contents in their newsletters. He asked staff to provide a report
  to add back a certain language omitted in 2019 Boards and Commission Code and to also
  revisit term limits. Asatryan seconded. Mayor Kassakhian asked to provide a report on the
  appointment process for the Boards and Commissions. Brotman seconded.

  Council Member Devine commended staff for a successful National Night Out event and
  thanked them for accompanying her in distributing the organic pails in several places.

  Mayor Kassakhian announced that schools start next week and reminded the public to be more
  patient during drop-offs and pick-ups. He wished the students good luck and a successful
  academic year. He attended the screening of a documentary called the “Motherland,” the Asian
  Hall of Fame event at the Alex Theatre, and the art exhibits at the Glendale Central Library.
  Kassakhian spoke about the pension review report which was discussed at the 2pm meeting
  earlier and asked to have another discussion at a regular council meeting. He asked staff to
  create a Civic Academy Program which will give residents a chance to have a deeper
  knowledge of the city and its operations. Devine seconded. He asked staff to bring back the
  Neighborhood Town Hall Meeting. Brotman seconded. Kassakhian asked staff to provide a brief
  report on the fiscal impact for the city paying the ballot statements of the candidates that ran this
  previous election cycle. Lastly, he asked council to adjourn in memory of Dr. Don Empey, a
  longtime deputy superintendent of the GUSD.
